chapter_theme: Siva knows those who love him (அன்பு செய்வாரை அறியும் சிவன்): he sees what each has spurned and gained and returns love with grace; siddhas cannot find him but he stands before devotees; claims to know him through love ring hollow without true understanding, and mingling with him inwardly is the true worship.
structure_note: Grace answering love (280 to 282); union with him as lovers' union (283); devotees against siddhas and against false claims (284, 286, 287); the poet's vision and inner worship (285, 288, 289).

280.reading: The Lord knows what we have spurned and what we have gained; the excellent Lord gives grace gladly, and to those who can love with tender, fresh love so that grace grows, his grace returns their love with delight.
280.nuance: கொழுந்தன்பு is love like a young shoot, fresh and growing. The chapter's title idea opens here: the Lord knows (அறியும்), so love is not unseen.

281.reading: Though the Lord made what suits a joyful birth and the toils of a sorrowful birth are many, this birth that the First Lord ordained by mingling in love is where births end.
281.nuance: அன்பிற் கலவிசெய்து (mingling in love) and முன்பு இப்பிறவி are compressed. One reading is that a birth lived in love with the Lord is the last birth; முடிவது may also mean simply 'is fulfilled'.

282.reading: The light that rises above a loving mind consents to accept the joyful garland; free of the tangle of the five sorrowful snares, seek the mind that is friendly to him.
282.nuance: கண்ணி means both garland and snare, and the verse uses both: the joyful garland of love offered to him, and the five snares that dance, traditionally the senses.

283.reading: For those who can subside into feeling as love settles on a woman in union, the joy of embracing him, delighting and moving beyond awareness, is like that.
283.nuance: Sexual union is the image for union with the Lord. உணர்ச்சியில்லாது (without awareness) is taken as loss of separate self-awareness. அதுவிது (that is this) leaves open which joy is the measure of the other.

284.reading: The siddhas, even with those close to him, have never discerned that fitting light; but to devotees who bowed and worshipped him in devotion he stood before them and gave release.
284.nuance: பத்திமை is bhakti, devotion. The contrast is pointed in a book that elsewhere honours siddhas: attainment does not find him, devotion does. உற்றுநின்றாரொடும் is unclear.

285.reading: I saw the feet of him with fragrant konrai, the twin anklets of him who wears the elephant's hide, the feet of him who dwells in the lotus; I saw the anklet within my love.
285.nuance: கண்டேன் opens every line. The one dwelling in the lotus is usually Brahma, but here may be Siva in the heart-lotus; the last line places the vision inside the poet's love.

286.reading: No one knows the Lover: Nambhan, whom the gods above hail as the leader who becomes things of many kinds, the joyful one who abides in joy and relishes it.
286.nuance: அன்பன் can be 'the one who loves' or 'the one loved'. இரதிக்கும் (relishes) gives the Lord himself as enjoying joy.

287.reading: Those who do not know their past births and deaths say 'we know the Lord through love', but they cannot know in love Nandi, who is joy and has no birth or death.
287.nuance: The verse sets the claimants' bondage to birth and death against Nandi's freedom from it. Whether it rejects their claim outright or says love alone is not enough without knowledge of bondage is unclear.

288.reading: The Lord knows those who night and day keep themselves in the bond and show him tender care; if they abide radiant and cease from action, the Lord comes and stands gathered among us.
288.nuance: பாசத்துள் வைத்து may mean in the bond of love, or, in Siddhanta language, while still in the fetters (பாசம்) that bind the soul. செயலற்றிருந்திடில் (becoming actionless) is taken as surrender or yogic stillness.

289.reading: Why let go of the excellent light and then grasp it again? I will hold to his endless greatness and follow it; to mingle in honey with the Lord who stands as my life is the sacred bath.
289.nuance: மஞ்சனம் is the ritual bathing of the image; the verse makes inner union the true ablution. மட்டு may be honey (of love) or measure, giving 'mingling without measure'.

links.note: 270 says those who know love is Siva rest as that love; 287 warns that people who claim to know him through love, while blind to their own births and deaths, do not.
Both set love above attainment: 272 says self-burning austerity does not reach him without love, 284 that the siddhas never discern him while devotees receive release.
